children: Nasdaq futures fell sharply as headwinds facing the artificial-intelligence trade returned to the forefront of investors' focus after Monday's Jensen Huang-powered market recovery faded.

Futures for all three major stock indexes were in the red. Nasdaq contracts were 2.8% lower, on track to wipe out the bounce the index received following Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia chief executive. Futures for the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1.9% and 0.4%, respectively.

Nvidia shares continued to weaken after their historic rally Monday, falling more than 5% in premarket trade. The chip company led premarket declines across AI-linked stocks, with big tech stocks including Meta and Apple also caught up in the selloff.

Even if earnings for semiconductor companies remain strong, investors are looking beyond results and focusing on concerns around the path to future monetization for the broader AI sector, Allianz strategists wrote in a note.

"The third-quarter earnings season has deepened investor skepticism toward the sustainability of hyperscalers' AI bets," they wrote. Hyperscalers are big tech companies that operate large networks of computing infrastructure.

Asian equities fell, with all major stock benchmarks in the continent closing lower. The threat of a fresh round of U.S. tariffs on China added to bearish AI sentiment. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer is expected to unveil the results of a monthslong tariff investigation into the industrial subsidies of China, the European Union and 14 other nations as soon as this week, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the plans.
European stocks reversed earlier gains as the market selloff intensified. The continent-wide Stoxx 600 fell 0.2%.

Oil prices also turned direction as the trading day progressed. Benchmark Brent crude contracts rose 0.8% to $92.20 a barrel after earlier trading below $90 a barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude rose 0.2% to $82.23 a barrel. Traders are weighing expectations of a global supply surplus ahead of an OPEC+ meeting this weekend.

Treasury yields fell ahead of Wednesday's personal consumption expenditures inflation data and the second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product. The fall in yields accelerated as investors sought refuge from losses in equity markets. Ten-year yields fell by 5.6 basis points to trade around 4.850%, while rate-sensitive two-year yields dropped by 6 basis points to trade around 4.610%.
Economists in a WSJ survey expect PCE data to show the annual core price index rose 3.2% in October from 3.1% in September.
The dollar strengthened against a basket of global currencies but remained shy of its 20-month high hit Monday. Gold contracts fell back toward $3,500, while bitcoin remained under $60,000.
As well as U.S. inflation and growth data, weekly jobless claims data will be published Wednesday ahead of the Thursday holiday. Investors will also look to the Federal Reserve's Beige Book.
